# GEO report: harbor-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 69/100, Needs work

Confidence: High (checked 25 of 25 points).
How it's calculated: low = 17.33 ÷ 25 × 100 = 69. High = (17.33 + 0) ÷ 25 × 100 = 69.

Everything could be settled from the code, so the score is a single number. The main losses are two AI-search crawlers blocked in `robots.txt`, broken structured data (JSON-LD, the machine-readable labels in the page), and one canonical address copied onto every page. These results are read from code, not measured on a live site.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Decide whether to unblock the AI search crawlers
- **Why it matters:** `OAI-SearchBot` (ChatGPT search) and `PerplexityBot` are barred from the whole site, so those tools can't read any page.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:4-8`
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: OAI-SearchBot` / `Disallow: /` and `User-agent: PerplexityBot` / `Disallow: /`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 81 (from 69). I assumed you want to be found, because there is no `geo.config.json` declaring a policy. If the block is deliberate, keep it and tell me. The GEO-009 rule would then be Not applicable, so it would drop out of the score instead of gaining points.

### 2. Repair the two broken structured data blocks
- **Why it matters:** Machines can't read invalid JSON-LD, so the FAQ and Article labels are lost.
- **Where:** `src/data/faq.json:8` and `src/pages/moorings.astro:9`
- **What the code says:** `" ": {` (it should be `"acceptedAnswer"`) and `"headline": "Moorings and prices", }` (a trailing comma makes the JSON invalid)
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 77 on its own, or 87 together with item 1.

### 3. Give each page its own canonical address
- **Why it matters:** `/moorings` and `/contact` both tell search engines the real page is the home page.
- **Where:** `src/layouts/Base.astro:8`
- **What the code says:** `<link rel="canonical" href="https://harbor.example/" />`
- **Size:** Small. Build the URL from `Astro.url.pathname` and a `site` setting in the Astro config.
- **Score after this:** 75 on its own. The three fixes together give 95.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid | Clear | `public/robots.txt`, valid lines, 3 of 3 |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have access | Problem | `public/robots.txt:4-8`, 2 crawlers blocked site-wide |
| GEO-014 | Routes are indexable | Clear | `/` and `/moorings` indexable. `/contact` is noindex, which looks deliberate (`src/pages/contact.astro:4`) |
| GEO-015 | Absolute canonical per page | Problem | `src/layouts/Base.astro:8`, 1 of 3 routes clear |
| GEO-003 | Content in server HTML | Clear | Astro static pages, no browser-only content fetching |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Problem | `src/data/faq.json:8` and `src/pages/moorings.astro:9`, 0 of 2 routes clear |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap discoverable | Clear | `public/sitemap.xml`, plus `Sitemap:` line at `robots.txt:10` |
| GEO-012 | Title, description, lang | Clear | `src/layouts/Base.astro:4-7`, unique per page |
| GEO-016 | Links in server HTML | Clear | `src/layouts/Base.astro:12`, plain `<a href>` |
| GEO-017 | No snippet restriction | Problem | `src/layouts/Base.astro:9`, 1 of 3 routes clear |
| GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Clear | Read `Base.astro` and `Newsletter.jsx`: labelled input, named button, no images |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | No app declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt | Not scored | Not present |
| GEO-102 | App structured data | Not scored | Not an app |

## Other problems found

- **A noindex page is listed in the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:5`: `<loc>https://harbor.example/contact</loc>`, while `src/pages/contact.astro:4` sets `robots="noindex"`. Remove it from the sitemap, or drop the noindex.
- **Snippet limit applies to nearly every page (also GEO-017):** `src/layouts/Base.astro:9`: `robots ?? "max-snippet:0"`. This default blocks text snippets site-wide. Change the fallback to `"index, follow"`. On the home page and `/moorings` it overrides a deliberate-looking setup and probably isn't intended.

## Worth considering

- **Label the harbour office as a business:** `src/pages/contact.astro:6`: `Call the harbour office on 01326 000000.` Adding LocalBusiness or Organization JSON-LD with name, phone and address might help machines identify who runs the site. Note that this page is noindex.
- **Fill out the moorings page:** `src/pages/moorings.astro:5`: `description="Mooring sizes and seasonal prices."` The page body has only one line (`Prices start at £40 a night.`), so add the sizes and seasonal prices it promises as text.
- **Put the FAQ answers on the page:** `src/pages/index.astro:8` emits the FAQ only as JSON-LD, so visitors never see "Can I book by the night?". Show the same Q&As as visible text.
- **Mark up the price:** `src/pages/moorings.astro:7`: `Prices start at £40 a night.` Offer or Product structured data could label it.
- **Link the pages to each other:** `src/pages/index.astro:7`: `Seasonal and visitor moorings, with a water taxi.` Link "moorings" to `/moorings` from the body text.
- **Add head basics:** `src/layouts/Base.astro:5-10` has no `charset`, `viewport` or social (Open Graph) tags, and pages have no `<main>` element.
- **Add `lastmod` dates:** `public/sitemap.xml:3-5` has none. Real dates might help crawlers.
- **Set the site URL in the Astro config:** the repo has no `astro.config`. Setting `site` would let Astro generate the sitemap and canonicals, in place of the hand-kept sitemap and hardcoded URLs.
- **Make the home page title clearer:** `src/pages/index.astro:5`: `title="Harbor moorings in Cornwall"` while the H1 says Falmouth. Name the harbour in the title.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Live status codes, redirects and headers:** a live scan with your URL would confirm these.

## Assumptions

- You want AI search tools to find this site (no `geo.config.json`). The `robots.txt` blocks are treated as unintended on that basis.
- The sample was all 3 routes (`/`, `/moorings`, `/contact`), the shared layout and navigation, the only component, `faq.json`, `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml`. JSON-LD sources: 2 found (`faq.json`, the inline Article). I searched for other JSON-LD and `noindex` sources.
- The `/contact` noindex is deliberate.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-015`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
